name: Phukha
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. De Gruyter (phonological profiles of Phula lects incl. Phukha)
earlier_scan.note: Paywalled monograph; Pelkey 2008 La Trobe dissertation not reachable

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-068 [phh] (submitted by Jamin R. Pelkey, adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International.
sources.note: No phonology; renames Phula > Phukha and cites Edmondson 2002, 2003, Fried 2000, Pelkey 2008.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: toward the synthesis and statement of a sub-branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. General Phula phonology remarks only: 'Most known Phula languages have a tense-lax phonation contrast, and some retain consonant finals. Phula languages usually have five tonemes and utilize contour tonal contrasts' (p. 58); footnote notes Fried (2000:27) lists a fifth glottalized tone for Phukhla while Edmondson (2003:308) interprets it differently.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2003. Three Tibeto-Burman languages of Vietnam. In Bradley, LaPolla, Michailovsky & Thurgood (eds), Language variation: papers on variation and change in the Sinosphere and in the Indosphere in honour of James A. Matisoff, 305-320. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 555.
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3 (pp. 307-310) on Phu Kha gives an initial inventory with dental/velar clusters, syllabic nasals, codas -p -n -ng, and lexical tones 31/35/33 (+ marginal 53) with pitch plots; a full-text search for stress/accent the whole chapter for stress/accent/prominence returns no hit.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2002. Phu Kha, Xá Phó, Mantsi, Coong, Sila, Lahu, Hani, and Proto-Loloish Data List. 88 pp. (formerlyhttp://ling.uta.edu/~jerry/tbv.pdf).
sources.note: Comparative wordlist only (Phu Kha column with tone numbers); no prose, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page phuk1235 and Wikipedia 'Phukha language'
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Wikipedia summarises 'five tones' from Fried 2000 and cites Fried 2000, Pelkey 2005, Ethnologue.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages: a study from the perspectives of shared innovation and phylogenetic estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Comparative work that uses Phukha data (from Fried/Edmondson); unlikely to state stress but the only other modern treatment that handles the language's phonology; cited by Glottolog for the classification.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. Trends in Linguistics: Studies and Monographs 229. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL3311.Y5 P45 2011) (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL3311.Y5 P45 2011
sources.note: Contains phonological profiles of all Phula lects including Phukha based on Pelkey's own fieldwork; the most authoritative modern synthesis and the source named by the earlier scan.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2008. The Phula languages in synchronic and diachronic perspective. PhD dissertation, La Trobe University. 439 pp.

sources.note: Dissertation version of Pelkey 2011 with the same phonological profiles; a La Trobe repository copy may be open even though the book is not.
